neighbours.label: function words and modifiers leading to a shoreline term in intertidal and coastal prose: 'at low (tide)', 'below the (tide mark)', 'ebb of the (tide)'; the same frames on land stay quiet
fire: The periwinkle clings to boulders exposed at low tide.
Bladder wrack grows thickly just below the high tide line.
Sea anemones shelter in pools at the edge of the ebb tide.
Oysters lie exposed by the retreating tide on the mudflats.
Clams bury themselves in sand near the low water mark.
Barnacles cover the pier pilings between the tide lines.
Eelgrass meadows thrive in the shallow bays along the estuary.
Dulse and kelp are gathered from the rocks at the turn of the tide.
quiet: The lizard clings to boulders exposed on the ridge.
Heather grows thickly just below the high mountain pass.
Field mice shelter in barns at the edge of the village.
Squirrels lie hidden in the branches above the orchard.
Beetles bury themselves in soil near the old fence post.
Posters cover the walls of the station's main corridor.
Wheat fields thrive on the broad plains along the railway.
Apples and pears are gathered from the trees at the end of summer.
